sections.html:
Murray occupies the core of the Salt Lake Valley and touches Taylorsville, Holladay, South Salt Lake, Millcreek and West Jordan. The Jordan River marks its western edge, and Big and Little Cottonwood Creeks both run through town to reach it. The 2020 count was 50,637 people, up from 46,746 in 2010.

Nearly two thirds of homes are lived in by their owners, which makes Murray a more owner-heavy market than some of its neighbors. A short summary of the housing picture follows.

Murray housing measureFigure
Households20,490
Owner-occupied housing rate64.7%
Median value of owner-occupied homes$507,500
Median gross rent$1,500
Median household income$90,746

The median value covers the whole city, so a particular house can sit well above or below it.

sections.h2: From smelter town to medical center
sections.html:
Settlers arrived in 1848, and the city incorporated on January 3, 1903. The smelting era ran from about 1870 until ASARCO's lead smelter closed in 1949, and the stacks came down in 2000. Intermountain Healthcare bought the site, and Intermountain Medical Center, which replaced Cottonwood Hospital in 2007, is now one of the city's largest employers.

Retail followed in the 1970s with Fashion Place Mall and a State Street lined with car dealerships. For a seller, the takeaway is simple: Murray is a long-established city with a large hospital campus nearby and a steady base of owner-occupied homes.

Murray runs its own police, fire, power, water, sewer, library and parks departments. In many areas it supplies power, water, sewer, garbage and stormwater service, though other providers cover properties where the city has no infrastructure. Murray City Power, publicly owned since 1913, serves about 18,000 customers.

  • Call the utility billing office at (801) 264-2626 to ask how a final reading and a transfer of service work for your address.
  • The office is at 10 East 4800 South, Suite 160.
  • Pay only through the city's own website, since look-alike sites target Murray customers.
  • Find out whether your water and sewer come from the city or another provider before you list.

Three light rail stations serve Murray: Murray North, Murray Central and Fashion Place West, on the Blue and Red lines. Murray Central is also where FrontRunner commuter rail, which opened in December 2012, meets TRAX, and it is the only such connection outside Salt Lake City. Interstate 15 and Interstate 215 both cross the city, and mean travel time to work is 20.7 minutes.

If your house is a short walk from a station, put that in the listing.

Murray has its own school district, though some addresses fall in Granite School District instead, so the school an address belongs to depends on the street. Confirm the zone before quoting it to a buyer.

  • Bergertown, south of 4800 South along Little Cottonwood Creek, began as a Swiss immigrant enclave.
  • The Murray Downtown Historic District follows State Street.
  • Murray City Park covers 22 acres with a baseball stadium and an amphitheatre.
  • The Jordan River Parkway trail runs along the western edge.

The city treats a residential rental as a business, so the owner needs a current Murray business license. One license covers every rental held by the same legal entity, and hiring a property manager does not replace it.

A license can't be moved between owners or addresses. A buyer who inherits your tenants must apply for a new one. Running a rental without a license, or after one lapses, brings a penalty of 100 percent of the past-due fees under City Code 5.04.280. Renewal notices go out on the first of the month the license expires, and a postmark does not prove timely receipt.

Each lot may have one accessory dwelling unit, and the owner must live in the main house or the unit. A detached unit needs a lot of at least 10,000 square feet, a height of 20 feet or less and a single story, and it can't sit in the front yard. Renting an ADU for stays shorter than 30 days is prohibited. Before the application is accepted, an affidavit on occupancy and short-term rental terms must be recorded with the Salt Lake County Recorder.

Murray shares the valley's earthquake exposure. The Wasatch Fault and soft lake sediments shape building risk across the Wasatch Front. The Salt Lake City segment last ruptured 1,200 to 1,300 years ago, and the chance of a magnitude 6.0 or larger quake within 50 years is put at 57 percent.

Expect an inspector to flag chimney bracing, an unstrapped water heater and foundation cracks. If the lot is near Big or Little Cottonwood Creek, ask the county for flood zone information.

Salt Lake County sets the dates for every Murray property. Value is measured as of January 1. Valuation notices go out in July and August, with a 45 day Board of Equalization window counted from the original mailing. Tax notices are mailed by November 1, the penalty-free payment deadline is November 30, and delinquency starts December 1.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Salt Lake County
sections.html: The county's 2024 recording requirements call for white 8.5 by 11 inch paper, a legible caption on the first page, the grantee's name and mailing address, and a legal description. The grantor's name must read the same on the title, the document, the notary acknowledgment and the signature. A flat $40 recording fee was listed, so confirm the amount before you sign. A title company normally handles all this for a sale.

sections.h2: If you are selling a rental in Murray
sections.html: Landlords have a few extra items to clear. Confirm the Murray business license is current, since a lapse carries a penalty on past-due fees. Collect the lease and rent roll for the buyer. If a detached unit was added, locate the recorded affidavit, because the buyer's title company will see it on file with the county. Where a tenant is staying, agree early on how and when the buyer takes over the lease so closing does not stall.

sections.h2: Selling a Murray house for cash
sections.html:
A cash sale still closes through a title company in the usual way, minus the buyer's lender. We look at the house as it stands, make an offer, and the title company takes care of the signing and the county recording.

  1. Tell us about the house, including tenants or an ADU if there is one.
  2. We review it and quote a price.
  3. You accept or decline, with no obligation either way.
  4. If you accept, the title company sets the closing.

Murray owners most often reach out about inherited homes, rentals with tenants and houses that need work. Bring the rental license if you have one, any ADU affidavit and the newest tax notice, and the process moves faster.

faqs.q: What school district is Murray, Utah in?
faqs.a: Most of the city is in Murray City School District. Granite School District serves some addresses, so check the district for a specific one.
Murray City Power, a municipal utility created in 1913, serves about 18,000 customers. The city also supplies water, sewer and garbage service in many areas.

faqs.q: Do I need a business license to rent out a Murray house?
faqs.a: Yes. One license covers all rentals owned by the same legal entity, and it can't be transferred to a buyer.

faqs.q: Can I rent an accessory dwelling unit short term in Murray?
faqs.a: No. Rentals shorter than 30 days are prohibited in an ADU, and the owner must live on the property.

faqs.q: When are Murray property taxes due?
faqs.a: Pay by November 30 to avoid a penalty. Unpaid taxes become delinquent on December 1.
